2.text: clothing of the deceased.¹ I would mention here that I was told that in
2.note: Footnote marker printed as a raised numeral 1 tight after the period; CATMuS read it as '!'. Keyed as U+00B9 SUPERSCRIPT ONE per §2.10.

3.text: olden times it was customary to eat the flesh of the one deceased, which,

4.text: for that purpose, was distributed among the nearest relatives. This flesh

5.text: was eaten mixed with tallow. Among the Yukaghir of the Kolyma, the

6.text: flesh and the bones of the deceased were also distributed among the relatives;

7.text: but, instead of being eaten, they were made into family amulets. Judging

8.text: by the accounts of the oldest inhabitants, leather bags filled with human

9.text: bones and dried flesh formed, up to comparatively recent times, the prin-
9.note: A small raised dot sits between 'and' and 'dried' at 2x, mid-height rather than baseline — not a letter or word, so per §2.14 it is a blot and keyed as nothing.

10.text: cipal sacred things of the family, even among the Russianized Yukaghir.

11.text: A bag of bones was called simply “grandfather,” and this “grandfather”
11.note: mz text carried a literal backslash-quote at line end; the raster shows the ordinary curly closing double quote (”), confirmed at 2x.

12.text: was supposed to afford to his descendants the most effective assistance. His

13.text: descendants appealed to him in the various affairs of their life, especially

14.text: when asking for success in hunting or for protection against an attack by
14.note: A baseline period sits between 'attack' and 'by' at 2x. With it removed the sentence reads cleanly into line 15 ('...against an attack by evil spirits.'); per §2.14 a punctuation-shaped error is a blot and keyed as nothing.

15.text: evil spirits. Similarly among the Chukchee, people in disastrous circumstances

16.text: sometimes seek relief from one of their dead. For instance, a Reindeer family,

17.text: a large part of whose herd has gone astray, will apply to the most respected

18.text: of all their dead ancestors, and the one who consequently receives most of

19.text: the sacrifices. They will request him to bring back the reindeer, and they

20.text: will promise him a fat buck or two in payment for his good services. “The

21.text: dead are always with us. They look upon us, and they may give us

22.text: protection,” said a Chukchee to me.

23.text: DECEASED AS ENEMIES. — Every variety of precaution and all the

24.text: protective incantations performed at the time of the funeral have had their

25.text: inception from the second point of view. These contradictory ideas about

26.text: the deceased are nevertheless very natural, and exist among many primitive

27.text: peoples. The natives, however, are conscious of the discrepancy between

28.text: the two points of view, and tried to explain it to me in their own way.

29.text: They said to me, “The deceased one, while he lies in the tent, is not

30.text: dangerous. He becomes bad, only when he is taken out into the wilderness,

31.text: whence he may come back a spirit.” And again: “The material objects
31.note: mz text carried a literal backslash-quote after 'spirit.'; the raster shows the ordinary curly closing double quote (”), confirmed at 2x.

32.text: connected with the deceased are not harmful. Only when he himself comes

33.text: back will he do harm. On the other hand, the deceased people come back

34.text: to us over and over again, countless times, through the womb of the woman.”
34.note: mz text carried a literal backslash-quote after 'woman.'; the raster shows the ordinary curly closing double quote (”), confirmed at 2x.

35.text: Others said, “Not all deceased persons will do harm. Only a part of

36.text: them bear ill-will toward living people: those will come back for harm. The

37.text: most dangerous are the double dead, the completely dead. They are beyond

38.text: being re-born into this world, and hence they become evil spirits in the other

39.text: world. They live on the very border of the country of the deceased people,
